Docs/Replay/Guide

Replay

Scheduled-input timing feedback

2 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓

Scheduled clients use timing feedback to keep inputs ahead of the authority without retaining an unnecessarily large prediction lead. The welcome exchange supplies a conservative initial prediction lead: the number of ticks the client simulates ahead of accepted authority state. It includes initial connection, application and checkpoint work, so it is not a permanent estimate of steady traffic. After admission, clients calibrate using the existing input_newest value in accepted snapshots. No protocol or checkpoint change is needed.

For each scheduled input tick, the client records the first successful transport submission time in a history-sized ring. A newer acknowledged input must match a retained entry from the current welcome/connection. Its elapsed time includes outbound queueing, server processing/snapshot cadence and return delivery: the metric is input turnaround, not pure transport RTT. Backpressured submissions are not timed, repeated windows retain the first successful time, and stale or missing entries do not produce estimates.

After three valid samples, the bootstrap lead becomes the recent turnaround peak converted to ticks plus four reserve ticks, clamped by configured lead, max_future - 2 and max_prediction - 2. A current one-second peak bucket and the preceding bucket retain short bursts while aging old peaks. lead_ticks remains the bound used to rebuild prediction after a complete ahead snapshot; it does not rewrite existing history or queued action/input ticks.

Clock discipline separately uses the server-observed arrival margin: input_newest - snapshot_tick. The target is three future input ticks. Around that target the existing ±2% correction is retained. Above seven ticks the clock runs at 0.9× until the excess drains; a negative margin uses 1.1× to recover. This changes future local stepping through the existing clock_scale API. It does not rewind or skip the authority, retime accepted requests, or bypass admission/fencing. Applications driving Client directly must apply clock_scale; the Godot Session adapter already does so. Spectators and latest-observation models keep scale 1.

Long local pump gaps invalidate outstanding samples, avoiding calibration from local suspension. The gap threshold is the larger of 250 ms and (snapshot_every + 2) / hz seconds. Reconnect, a new authority and every accepted Welcome reset timing history. Configured minimum lead still applies; it remains an application envelope choice rather than a universal latency recommendation.

Inspect input_timing.turnaround_ms, input_timing.arrival_lead, lead_ticks, clock_scale, and the cumulative Stats.timing_samples, timing_rejected and lead_updates. None is simulation state. The send-time ring adds one bounded Input_Sent record per history slot (24 bytes per slot on the tested arm64 build).

Tests include a delayed welcome that initially selects 62 ticks, changing latency and jitter, unchanged queued action due ticks, convergence, backpressure, local stalls, reconnect and non-scheduled clients. This policy does not promise zero corrections or hide link failure; ordinary history/capacity/recovery bounds remain.
